excerpt: Matik automatically builds personalised presentations and documents from live company data in Google Slides or PowerPoint. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz.
content:
Matik makes software that generates data-driven content automatically. Sales, customer success and marketing teams set up governed templates once; Matik then fills them with live data from sources such as a CRM or a data warehouse and produces native Google Slides or PowerPoint decks and other formats for each account. Typical outputs include quarterly business reviews, pricing proposals, renewal decks and personalised outreach. Its website, now at matik.ai, describes AI that builds the setup, structure, narrative and personalisation of a deck, while keeping figures grounded in real data queries and brand-approved templates. Content can be created from Matik's own interface, from the CRM or from Slack, and generation can be triggered by signals or schedules.

TechCrunch reported in 2021 that Matik was founded in 2019 by Nikola Mijic, its CEO, and Zak Stein, an early Box employee, and that it was based in San Francisco. Customers named at the time included Glassdoor, KeepTruckin, Handshake and Hover.

Funding

In October 2021 Matik raised a $20 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Menlo Ventures, BoxGroup and Oceans Ventures, bringing total funding to just over $23 million, according to TechCrunch. Menlo Ventures, one of its investors, explained its investment in a post on its website.

Pricing

Matik does not publish prices on its website. Companies book a demo for a quote.

Who it suits

Matik suits sales, customer success and revenue operations teams that build many similar data-heavy decks, such as QBRs and proposals, and want them consistent and on brand. Teams that make a few one-off presentations may not need automation.

We have not tested Matik. This page is based on Matik's website, TechCrunch and Menlo Ventures.
